text: Wahoo's Fish Taco is a U.S.-based restaurant chain that serves Mexican food blended with Brazilian and Asian flavors, categorized as a "fast casual restaurant" with food quality and preparation time between fast food and formal dining. The chain offers numerous vegetarian and some vegan options, including tofu, banzai veggies, and brown rice, and features a kids' meal menu. Wahoo's serves wahoo fish and Mahi-mahi in its tacos. Founded in 1988 in Costa Mesa, California, by Chinese-Brazilian brothers Eduardo "Ed" Lee, Renato "Mingo" Lee, and Wing Lam, the restaurant was inspired by traditional Chinese and Brazilian flavors combined with dishes the brothers encountered in Mexico. Their parents fled China in the 1950s, settled in São Paulo, Brazil, and had five sons born there; their father, Cheong Lee, and the eldest son moved to the U.S. in 1964, with the rest of the family arriving in 1975 to open Shanghai Pine Gardens on Balboa Island. The parents required their children to study medicine, law, or engineering; the eldest went to law school, the second to medicine, and Wing Lam initially studied engineering at San Diego State University before switching to finance after academic probation. The first Wahoo's location, at 1862 Placentia Avenue in Costa Mesa, opened in November 1988 and served Baja California-style fish tacos. The three brothers were the primary employees, with Wing Lam recalling in 2011 that he took orders, prepared them, and delivered them directly to tables. The brothers remain involved in daily operations, with Wing Lam serving as the public face of the company in public relations and marketing, and also staffing the California-based food truck. The first restaurant was funded in part by $30,000 from their parents after selling Shanghai Pine Gardens. Steve Karfaridis, the first manager of the second location in Laguna Beach, is now a business partner. The corporate headquarters are in Santa Ana, California. Projected sales in 2004 were $35,000,000 (equivalent to $58,270,000 in 2024), and by 2011, annual sales exceeded $60,000,000 (equivalent to $83,870,000 in 2024). By 1994, Wahoo's had opened two additional locations—one in Costa Mesa and one in Laguna Beach—and faced delays in securing a permit for a fourth location in Huntington Beach due to a city code requirement to pay for 12 parking spaces, leading to an additional location opening in Lake Forest in May 1994. By late 1995, the chain had six locations: five in Orange County, California, and one in Denver, Colorado. The Manhattan Beach location, opened in 1998, was the first outside Orange County. In 2001, Wahoo's had 22 locations and announced plans to open 40 more by 2006. By 2005, the chain had 36 locations, including the original Costa Mesa restaurant. Wahoo's has expanded across California and into Colorado, Hawaii, Nebraska, Nevada, New Jersey, and Pennsylvania. In 2009, the company announced plans to add 100 franchise locations by 2014, though those plans have slowed. On its 25th anniversary in 2013, Wahoo's had 64 restaurants in seven states and opened its first international location in Tokyo, Japan. On April 12, 2020, Wahoo's delivered 300 meals to an Irvine hospital as part of the California Love Drop initiative, a collaboration between Wing Lam and partners to support frontline workers during the COVID-19 pandemic, which has since delivered over 11,000 meals. From the beginning, Wahoo's targeted the surfing community with affordable prices and eclectic decor featuring stickers and surfing equipment, catering to corporate events and local surf contests to build word-of-mouth, and similarly engaged other extreme sports communities like snowboarding, rock climbing, and cycling. The chain built a youth following by naming a local "athlete of the week" and sponsoring a meal that drew the athlete's friends. The fish tacos sold by street vendors in Baja California were traditionally filled with unsaleable by-caught fish like shark, which were deep-fried and served with cabbage and tomatoes. While at San Diego State, Wing Lam developed the idea to create a healthier, grilled fish taco for American consumers, similar to the origin story of Ralph Rubio’s Rubio’s, differing in that Wahoo's used grilled meat instead of fried and beans without lard or bacon fat, and included vegetarian and vegan options. This approach aligned with a growing consumer interest in "fresh" Mexican cuisine, and Wahoo's has provided nutritional information from the start to appeal to health-conscious customers. The chain is credited as one of the earliest creators of an Asian-taco fusion. Word-of-mouth supported new Orange County openings, but when expanding to Manhattan Beach, marketing shifted to local newspaper and school advertising. Author Earlene Fowler credited the original Wahoo's location as her office while writing her first novel. January 9, 2013 was declared Wahoo's Fish Taco Day in Costa Mesa to celebrate the chain's 25th anniversary. In 2004, Travis Barker, drummer for blink-182, opened a Wahoo's Fish Taco in Norco, California, co-owned with the Lee brothers.
